name: PGSTY Silo
summary: A community-maintained fork of the open-source MinIO server, with builds, images, security fixes and the full web console.
intro: Silo is the open-source MinIO server, kept alive. When MinIO, Inc. stopped shipping community binaries and archived the `minio/minio` repository, the Pigsty project, which uses MinIO to store PostgreSQL backups, forked it and kept one release line going: prebuilt binaries, multi-arch container images, RPM, DEB and APK packages, security fixes, and the web admin console that upstream had removed from the community build.

It is meant as a drop-in replacement. The S3 API, the `MINIO_*` environment variables, metrics, routes and the on-disk format are unchanged, so the same disks can move from MinIO to Silo without copying data or rewriting metadata. What changes is the packaging: the server binary is called `silo`, images live at `docker.io/pgsty/silo`, and the default config directory is `~/.silo`. The image still accepts `minio server /data` as a command, and it ships the `mc` client.
strengths: The closest replacement for MinIO: same S3 API, same `MINIO_*` settings, same data on disk
Prebuilt binaries, packages and images again, including on Docker Hub
Restores the full web console (users, policies, buckets, metrics) that the community build lost
AGPLv3 with no CLA: contributions stay with their authors, so no single company can relicense it
limits: Young and maintained by a small community, so check its release cadence and security advisories yourself
No mixed MinIO and Silo cluster: upgrade every node to Silo in one go, not as a rolling upgrade
Scripts that call `/usr/bin/minio` or use the `minio/minio` image name need updating
Inherits MinIO’s AGPLv3 obligations if you modify it and offer it over a network

values: `docker.io/pgsty/silo`; `minio server` still works as the command

story: Pigsty, an open-source PostgreSQL distribution, had used MinIO as the place to keep database backups. Through 2025 MinIO, Inc. pulled back from the community edition: the admin console was cut down to an object browser, then in October 2025 the project switched to source-only releases with no prebuilt binaries, and in December it went into maintenance mode. Pigsty’s maintainers forked the server and published their first build in December 2025.

The fork’s stated motive is practical rather than ideological. Its manifesto says that if upstream restores its community edition, the fork will narrow its scope and offer its fixes back. Until then it keeps one maintained line of the AGPLv3 server: builds, packages, images, security fixes and the full console.

Upstream archived `minio/minio` in April 2026. In August 2026 the fork renamed itself from `pgsty/minio` to Silo, renaming the product and its binaries and images but, in its own words, not “the protocol and your data”.

choices.choice: Keep the protocol, data and settings; rename the product
choices.why: Users needed to keep their disks and configuration, but a fork can’t use MinIO’s trademarks. So the S3 API, `MINIO_*` variables and on-disk format stay, while the binary, image and console are renamed.

Without copyright assignment no single entity owns all of the code, so the AGPLv3 can’t be changed later. MinIO, Inc., which did hold the copyright, had already relicensed the server once, from Apache 2.0 to AGPLv3 in 2021.
In 2025 the community build lost its admin console, leaving an object browser and the `mc` command line. Users complained, and the fork put the full console back.

timeline.text: Admin console removed from MinIO’s community build
MinIO goes source-only (October); Pigsty forks the server
First fork release, `RELEASE.2025-12-03T12-00-00Z`, published in December
Fork renamed from `pgsty/minio` to Silo on 6 August
